newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brittan says China needs new WTO entry plan.
newsitem.headline: Brittan says China needs new WTO entry plan.

text.p: European Trade Commisisoner Sir Leon Brittan said on Friday China needed to produce a new and ambitious plan for entry to the World Trade Organisation.

Brittan said European Union officials had held useful discussions with Chinese officials this week on the fringes of the WTO's ministerial conference on the question of its long-running bid to join the 128-member world trade watchdog.

"We all want Chinese membership as quickly as possible. We intend to intensify our bilateral as well as Geneva-based talks in the months ahead," Brittan, who negotiates on trade issues on behalf of the 15-member EU, told a news conference.
"The speed of progress, though, depends not only on us but on China's ability to produce new, more detailed and more ambitious proposals.

"I call on our Chinese partners to join us in a major effort in the months ahead. If China produces a sensible, positive package, we would be ready to see it implemented over a transitional period -- which has been the essential European concept that I've put forward many times," Brittan added.

China has been pushing to enter the WTO on the favourable terms granted to developing nations, but many Western countries, most notably the United States, insist China's economy is too large for such treatment.
